'''Oluwole Talabi''' {{Audio|LL-Q34311 (yor)-Tunmise123-Oluwole Talabi.wav|Listen|help=no}}(born 28 February 1986) is a Nigerian [[science fiction]] writer, engineer, and editor,<ref name="STH">{{cite magazine |last=Ryman |first=Geoff |author-link=Geoff Ryman |date=7 February 2019 |title=Wole Talabi: 100 AFRICAN WRITERS OF SFF – PART THIRTEEN: THE TRAVELERS |url=http://strangehorizons.com/non-fiction/wole-talabi/ |url-access=limited |magazine=[[Strange Horizons]] |location=Lagos |page=13 |issue=100 |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |url=https://vector-bsfa.com/2020/04/29/the-big-idea-an-interview-with-wole-talabi/ |title="The big idea": An interview with Wole Talabi |first=Jo Lindsay |last=Walton |author-link=Jo Walton |date=29 April 2020 |access-date=1 October 2021 |magazine=[[Vector (journal)|Vector]] |issue=289}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |first1=Silvia |last1=Moreno-Garcia |first2=Lavie |last2=Tidhar |date=21 May 2021 |title=A magical selection of African speculative fiction |url=https://borneobulletin.com.bn/a-magical-selection-of-african-speculative-fiction/ |access-date=1 October 2021 |newspaper=[[Borneo Bulletin|Borneo Bulletin Online]] |language=en-US}}</ref> who is considered among the [[Third Generation of Nigerian Writers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thisdaylive.com/index.php/2022/01/23/new-nigerian-literatures-unsung-heroes/ |title=New Nigerian Literature Unsung Heroes |first=Chukwuebuka |last=Umezurike |date=23 January 2022  |access-date=23 January 2022|newspaper=[[This Day]]}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Talabi was raised in [[Warri]], [[Delta State|Delta]], a city in southern Nigeria, where his father was a chemical engineer, before later moving to [[Benin City]] and then later [[Lagos]].<ref name="STH"/><ref name=":0" /> He studied chemical engineering at [[Obafemi Awolowo University]] and earned a master's degree with distinction at [[Imperial College London]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Talabi then worked as an engineer, and partway through his career began to write professionally. He stated that he had never been formally trained in writing except for two online classes from the [[University of Edinburgh]] and the [[University of Michigan]], but he had written stories since learning to read as a child.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sorg |first=Arley |date=February 2024 |title=When the World Changes: A Conversation with Wole Talabi |url=https://clarkesworldmagazine.com/talabi_interview/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Clarkesworld Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>

His works include an amount of short stories; the anthologies ''These Words Expose Us: An Anthology'' (2014), ''Lights Out: Resurrection'' (2016), ''[[Africanfuturism: An Anthology]]'' (2020).

''Incomplete Solutions'', published in 2019, was Talabi's first published collection of short stories, covering five years of his writing. The stories are from a range of speculative genres but also include non-speculative romance, and they explore contradicting philosophies and levels of hope, but often have themes of choice and identity. They embed Nigerian culture and perspectives without explaining them to unfamiliar readers. Adri Joy, reviewing for ''[[Strange Horizons]]'', praised the intriguing, fun and varied nature of the stories, while wishing for fewer male-centered or chauvinistic perspectives.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joy |first=Adri |date=2020-07-20 |title=Incomplete Solutions by Wole Talabi |url=http://strangehorizons.com/wordpress/non-fiction/incomplete-solutions-by-wole-talabi/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Strange Horizons |language=en}}</ref>

Talabi published his debut novel ''[[Shigidi and the Brass Head of Obalufon]]'' in 2023.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Kluwe |first=Chris |date=2023-08-24 |title=Book Review: Shigidi and the Brass Head of Obalufon by Wole Talabi |url=https://www.lightspeedmagazine.com/nonfiction/book-review-shigidi-and-the-brass-head-of-obalufon-by-wole-talabi-2/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Lightspeed Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> Shigidi is a Yoruba god of nightmares who wants to get out of his minimum wage job at the Orisha Spirit Company. Shigidi's lover Nneoma, a succubus, helps him pull off a heist so he can leave: they have been tasked with stealing back the heavily protected brass head of Obalufon from the British Museum.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Wolfe |first=Gary K. |date=2023-09-19 |title=Gary K. Wolfe Reviews Shigidi and the Brass Head of Obalufon by Wole Talabi |url=https://locusmag.com/review/gary-k-wolfe-reviews-shigidi-and-the-brass-head-of-obalufon-by-wole-talabi/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Locus Online |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Chris Kluwe]], reviewing for ''[[Lightspeed (magazine)|Lightspeed]]'', praised the novel and said the pair's relationship and themes of capitalism and colonialism drive the story.<ref name=":1" /> Gary K. Wolfe, reviewing for ''Locus'', praised the book's balance of genre elements, keeping the "kinetic mix of ''noir'' heist fiction, erotic romance, political intrigue, and supernatural fireworks without distracting too much from the genuinely affecting relationship between Nneoma and Shigidi."<ref name=":2" /> Architra Mittra, for ''Strange Horizons'', also praised the book's balance of genre and its entertaining exploration of heavy themes, but criticized the stereotypical elements of the main relationship.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mittra |first=Archita |date=2023-11-08 |title=Shigidi and the Brass Head of Obalufon by Wole Talabi |url=http://strangehorizons.com/wordpress/non-fiction/shigidi-and-the-brass-head-of-obalufon-by-wole-talabi/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Strange Horizons |language=en}}</ref>

''Convergence Problems'', a collection released in 2024, focused on more traditional science fiction themes, with ideas, characterization, and Nigerian culture driving the pieces.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wolfe |first=Gary K. |date=2024-03-06 |title=Gary K. Wolfe Reviews Convergence Problems by Wole Talabi |url=https://locusmag.com/review/gary-k-wolfe-reviews-convergence-problems-by-wole-talabi/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Locus Online |language=en-US}}</ref>

He was described in ''[[Scientific American]]'' as "an author who blends [[transhumanism]] and the [[Turing test]]".<ref>{{cite news |title=Exploring Black Sci-Fi, Learning through Color, the Cost of Cooling, and Other New Books |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/exploring-black-sci-fi-learning-through-color-the-cost-of-cooling-and-other-new-books/ |author=Brady, Amy |date=1 July 2021 |newspaper=[[Scientific American]] |access-date=1 October 2021}}</ref>

Talabi has been a manager of a database of [[speculative fiction]] by African authors on the African Speculative Fiction Society website.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ryman |first=Geoff |date=2018-10-26 |title=Endnote: Afro-? African-? Astro-? |url=http://strangehorizons.com/wordpress/non-fiction/endnote-afro-african-astro/ |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=Strange Horizons |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=List of Published African SFF |url=https://www.africansfs.com/resources/list-of-published-african-sff |access-date=2025-09-13 |website=African Speculative Fiction Society |language=en-US}}</ref> Talabi is a founding charter member of the society.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Press Pack |url=https://www.africansfs.com/resources/press-pack |access-date=2022-07-01 |website=www.africansfs.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He married Rocío Vizuete Fernandez in 2023 in [[Madrid]], Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://brittlepaper.com/2023/08/wole-talabi-ties-the-knot-in-spain/|title=Nigerian Speculative Fiction Author Wole Talabi Ties the Knot in Beautiful Summer Wedding|website=[[Brittle Paper]]|last=Ghosh|first=Kuhelika|date=25 August 2023|access-date=13 April 2024}}</ref> Talabi has previously lived in [[Mexico]], [[England]], and [[Malaysia]].<ref name=":0" />

After winning his third Nommo Award in 2024, and having won in all three prose categories, he announced that he would decline any future nominations to clear the field for new writers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://file770.com/2024-nommo-awards/|title=2024 Nommo Awards|date=10 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://wtalabi.wordpress.com/2024/08/14/drink-and-drop-the-cup-my-nommo-award-acceptance-speech-or-something-like-it/|title=Drink And Drop The Cup: My Nommo Award Acceptance Speech, Or Something Like It.|date=14 August 2024}}</ref>

===Short Fiction===
